page: Amazon Web Services r8a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server type running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9R45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs without multithreading (1 thread per core). Memory configuration includes 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware platform includes support for AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16), hardware cryptography acceleration, and a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. There is no bundled GPU hardware, and local ephemeral storage is not provided.

Benchmark results show top-tier computational and throughput capabilities. Single-core performance registers within the top 10% across stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations, reaching 3,763.29 in stress-ng and 2,834.0 in Geekbench single-core tests. Multi-core performance is equally robust, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 27,850.0 and a Clang compilation score of 58,298.0. In memory throughput, the instance achieved 218.68 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 136.6 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth, alongside a top-tier score of 41,052.22 in PassMark database operations and 103.4 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. For machine learning tasks, it demonstrates top-tier CPU inference speeds on small models, handling 5,634.87 prompt tokens per second and 416.67 generation tokens per second.

Qualitatively, the r8a.8xlarge offers strong compute and memory density, making it cost-efficient for heavy data operations that demand wide memory bandwidth and dedicated execution cores. However, relying entirely on network-attached storage requires factoring in external storage configurations for persistent disk needs. The instance is well matched for in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, intensive compression routines, and CPU-driven language model inference.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring a 32-core AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with a 4.5 GHz clock speed, 32 dedicated vCPUs, and 256.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and hardware cryptography, along with a baseline network speed of 15 Gbps. The instance omits local storage and dedicated GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-core compute, high Clang compilation throughput, and exceptional database performance, achieving 103.4 million Redis SET operations per second and 218.68 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Its dense memory ratio of 8.0 GB per core and top-tier CPU inference capabilities make it well-suited for in-memory caching systems, distributed data analytics, and CPU-based model serving.

256.0 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 memory (8 GB per vCPU)
